spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m6p3t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Rooms    == {"orA", "orB"}
Surgeons == {"s1", "s2"}
LeaseLen == 2
MaxClock == 3

VARIABLES leases, clock, active

Lease(r, o, d) == [room |-> r, owner |-> o, deadline |-> d]

TypeInv ==
    /\ leases \subseteq [room: Rooms, owner: Surgeons, deadline: 0..(MaxClock+LeaseLen)]
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ active \subseteq Rooms

Init ==
    /\ leases = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ active = Rooms

RoomHeld(r) == \E l \in leases : l.room = r

Acquire(o, r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ ~RoomHeld(r)
    /\ leases' = leases \cup {Lease(r, o, clock + LeaseLen)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, active>>

Release(o, r) ==
    /\ Lease(r, o, clock + LeaseLen) \in leases \/ \E l \in leases : l.room = r /\ l.owner = o
    /\ leases' = {l \in leases : ~(l.room = r /\ l.owner = o)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, active>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ leases' = {l \in leases : l.deadline > clock + 1}
    /\ UNCHANGED active

Deactivate(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ active' = active \ {r}
    /\ leases' = {l \in leases : l.room # r}
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Reactivate(r) ==
    /\ r \notin active
    /\ active' = active \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leases, clock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Surgeons, r \in Rooms : Acquire(o, r) \/ Release(o, r)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Deactivate(r) \/ Reactivate(r)

NoDoubleBooking ==
    \A l1, l2 \in leases : l1.room = l2.room => l1.owner = l2.owner

vars == <<leases, clock, active>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleBooking
INVARIANT TypeInv
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler hands out short-lived leases on operating
rooms to surgeons. When a surgeon acquires a room, the lease is stamped with a
deadline a fixed number of clock ticks in the future; the surgeon owns that room
only until the lease expires. A background clock advances one tick at a time, and
an expiry sweep removes every lease whose deadline has passed, freeing the room.
A surgeon may voluntarily release a room before its lease expires. The hospital
can also change capacity at runtime by taking a room out of service; any lease on
a room that is deactivated is revoked immediately. Because leases expire on their
own and capacity can shrink, the scheduler must never let two different surgeons
believe they own the same operating room at the same instant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No operating room is ever held under active leases by two different surgeons at the same time.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m0p5t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
Jobs      == {"j1", "j2"}
Instances == {"i1", "i2"}

VARIABLES status, ver, seen, prints

TypeInv ==
    /\ status \in [Jobs -> {"pending", "done"}]
    /\ ver \in [Jobs -> 0..3]
    /\ seen \in [Instances -> [Jobs -> 0..3]]
    /\ prints \in Seq(Jobs)

Init ==
    /\ status = [j \in Jobs |-> "pending"]
    /\ ver = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
    /\ seen = [i \in Instances |-> [j \in Jobs |-> 0]]
    /\ prints = << >>

Snapshot(i, j) ==
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![i][j] = ver[j]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, ver, prints>>

Commit(i, j) ==
    /\ status[j] = "pending"
    /\ seen[i][j] = ver[j]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![j] = "done"]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![j] = ver[j] + 1]
    /\ prints' = Append(prints, j)
    /\ UNCHANGED seen

Retry(i, j) ==
    /\ seen[i][j] # ver[j]
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![i][j] = ver[j]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, ver, prints>>

Next ==
    \E i \in Instances, j \in Jobs :
        Snapshot(i, j) \/ Commit(i, j) \/ Retry(i, j)

EachJobPrintedOnce ==
    \A a, b \in DOMAIN prints : prints[a] = prints[b] => a = b

vars == <<status, ver, seen, prints>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT EachJobPrintedOnce
INVARIANT TypeInv
nl:
A print shop runs two independent spooler instances that share a single pool of
print jobs. There is no central lock server; instead each instance uses optimistic
concurrency. To print a job an instance first snapshots the job's current version
number, then attempts to commit the print only if the version it saw still matches
the live version. If another instance printed the job in between, the versions no
longer match and the commit is rejected, so the instance must re-snapshot and retry
against the now-updated record. Physically printing a job is irreversible: paper is
consumed and cannot be un-printed. Because two instances race over the same pool,
the danger is that the optimistic protocol lets a job slip through and be physically
printed twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No print job is ever physically printed more than once.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m8p2t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Trays == {"t1", "t2"}
Batch == 2
Total == 6

VARIABLES pool, trays, spoolLock, trayLock

TypeInv ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ trays \in [Trays -> 0..Total]
    /\ spoolLock \in {"free", "held"}
    /\ trayLock \in [Trays -> {"free", "held"}]

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ trays = [t \in Trays |-> 0]
    /\ spoolLock = "free"
    /\ trayLock = [t \in Trays |-> "free"]

TakeSpool ==
    /\ spoolLock = "free"
    /\ spoolLock' = "held"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, trays, trayLock>>

TakeTray(t) ==
    /\ spoolLock = "held"
    /\ trayLock[t] = "free"
    /\ trayLock' = [trayLock EXCEPT ![t] = "held"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, trays, spoolLock>>

FeedTray(t) ==
    /\ trayLock[t] = "held"
    /\ pool >= Batch
    /\ pool' = pool - Batch
    /\ trays' = [trays EXCEPT ![t] = trays[t] + Batch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spoolLock, trayLock>>

ReturnPool(t) ==
    /\ trayLock[t] = "held"
    /\ trays[t] >= Batch
    /\ trays' = [trays EXCEPT ![t] = trays[t] - Batch]
    /\ pool' = pool + Batch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spoolLock, trayLock>>

ReleaseLocks(t) ==
    /\ trayLock' = [trayLock EXCEPT ![t] = "free"]
    /\ spoolLock' = "free"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, trays>>

AdminForce(t) ==
    /\ pool >= Batch
    /\ pool' = pool - Batch
    /\ trays' = [trays EXCEPT ![t] = trays[t] + Batch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spoolLock, trayLock>>

Next ==
    \/ TakeSpool
    \/ \E t \in Trays : TakeTray(t) \/ FeedTray(t) \/ ReturnPool(t) \/ ReleaseLocks(t) \/ AdminForce(t)

PaperConserved == pool + trays["t1"] + trays["t2"] = Total

vars == <<pool, trays, spoolLock, trayLock>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PaperConserved
INVARIANT TypeInv
nl:
A print shop tracks sheets of paper as they move through a spooler with a two-level
hierarchical lock. All paper starts in a central pool. To feed paper into one of the
printer trays a worker must first take the coarse spooler lock and then the fine lock
on the specific tray, after which a batch of sheets moves from the pool into that
tray; sheets can also be returned from a tray back to the pool under the same locks.
A privileged shop administrator holds an override that can force a batch of sheets
between the pool and a tray without acquiring the locks, used to clear jams. Every
sheet of paper is either in the pool or in exactly one tray -- nothing is created or
destroyed by any move, whether locked or forced by the admin override. The total
number of sheets in the shop must stay constant across all operations.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of paper sheets across the pool and all trays is always exactly the starting total.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m8p5t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Patrons == {"p1", "p2"}
Books   == {"b1", "b2"}
Shelf(b) == "shelfX"

VARIABLES shelfLock, bookLock, loan

TypeInv ==
    /\ shelfLock \in [{"shelfX"} -> Patrons \cup {"free"}]
    /\ bookLock \in [Books -> Patrons \cup {"free"}]
    /\ loan \in [Patrons -> Books \cup {"none"}]

Init ==
    /\ shelfLock = [s \in {"shelfX"} |-> "free"]
    /\ bookLock = [b \in Books |-> "free"]
    /\ loan = [p \in Patrons |-> "none"]

LockShelf(p) ==
    /\ shelfLock["shelfX"] = "free"
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT !["shelfX"] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, loan>>

LockBook(p, b) ==
    /\ shelfLock["shelfX"] = p
    /\ bookLock[b] = "free"
    /\ bookLock' = [bookLock EXCEPT ![b] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, loan>>

Checkout(p, b) ==
    /\ bookLock[b] = p
    /\ loan[p] = "none"
    /\ \A q \in Patrons : loan[q] # b
    /\ loan' = [loan EXCEPT ![p] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, bookLock>>

ReturnAndUnlock(p, b) ==
    /\ loan[p] = b
    /\ loan' = [loan EXCEPT ![p] = "none"]
    /\ bookLock' = [bookLock EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT !["shelfX"] = "free"]

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : LockShelf(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : LockBook(p, b) \/ Checkout(p, b) \/ ReturnAndUnlock(p, b)

NoConcurrentLoan ==
    \A p, q \in Patrons : (loan[p] # "none" /\ loan[p] = loan[q]) => p = q

vars == <<shelfLock, bookLock, loan>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoConcurrentLoan
nl:
A library reservation system uses a two-level hierarchical locking discipline. To
check out a book a patron must first take the coarse lock on the shelf the book sits
on, and only then the fine lock on the individual book. Checking out a book is an
irreversible commitment for the duration of the loan: once issued to a patron the
copy is physically gone from the shelf until it is returned. Patrons may be slow --
they can hold locks and pause between steps -- but they never fail outright, so a
held lock is always eventually released by its owner. A patron releases both locks
after either completing or abandoning a checkout. The system must guarantee that,
however slowly patrons proceed through the lock hierarchy, a single book copy is
never on loan to two patrons at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A single book copy is never simultaneously on loan to two different patrons.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m2p6t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Participants == {"pa", "pb"}
MaxRound     == 2

VARIABLES round, phase, votes, decision

TypeInv ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ phase \in {"voting", "decided"}
    /\ votes \subseteq [who: Participants, rnd: 0..MaxRound, choice: {"commit", "abort"}]
    /\ decision \in {"none", "commit", "abort"}

Init ==
    /\ round = 0
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ decision = "none"

CastVote(p, c) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A v \in votes : v.who # p
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {[who |-> p, rnd |-> round, choice |-> c]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, decision>>

Decide ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A p \in Participants : \E v \in votes : v.who = p
    /\ decision' = IF \A v \in votes : v.choice = "commit" THEN "commit" ELSE "abort"
    /\ phase' = "decided"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, votes>>

AdminAbort ==
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ decision' = "none"

Reopen ==
    /\ phase = "decided"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ decision' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED round

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Participants, c \in {"commit", "abort"} : CastVote(p, c)
    \/ Decide
    \/ AdminAbort
    \/ Reopen

NoStaleVoteCounted == \A v \in votes : v.rnd = round

vars == <<round, phase, votes, decision>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleVoteCounted
INVARIANT TypeInv
nl:
A stock exchange decides each opening-auction cross with a two-phase commit across
its clearing participants. The coordinator opens a numbered voting round and asks the
participants to vote to commit or abort the cross; a decision is finalized only after
votes are gathered. Participants are tagged with the round they belong to, and a
privileged exchange administrator may abort the current round outright, which bumps
the round number and discards any votes already collected. The hazard is staleness:
a participant left over from a previous round could submit a vote that no longer
applies. The protocol must only ever count votes stamped with the current round, so
that no stale or unauthorized participant from an old round can influence the cross
that is being decided now.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every vote recorded for the current cross carries the current round number, so no stale-round vote is ever counted.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m3p4t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
Engines == {"e1", "e2", "e3"}
Orders  == {"o1", "o2", "o3"}
Cap     == 2

VARIABLES leader, alive, book

TypeInv ==
    /\ leader \in Engines \cup {"none"}
    /\ alive \subseteq Engines
    /\ book \subseteq Orders

Init ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ alive = Engines
    /\ book = {}

Elect(e) ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ e \in alive
    /\ leader' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, book>>

Admit(o) ==
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ Cardinality(book) < Cap
    /\ book' = book \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Crash(e) ==
    /\ e \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {e}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = e THEN "none" ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED book

Failover(e) ==
    /\ leader \notin alive
    /\ e \in alive
    /\ leader' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, book>>

Recover(e) ==
    /\ e \notin alive
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, book>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Engines : Elect(e) \/ Crash(e) \/ Failover(e) \/ Recover(e)
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Admit(o)

CapacityRespected == Cardinality(book) <= Cap

vars == <<leader, alive, book>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction on a cluster of matching engines. One
engine is elected leader and is solely responsible for admitting incoming orders
into the auction order book, which has a strictly bounded capacity. Any engine may
crash silently at any time: it simply stops responding and is dropped from the set
of live engines, with no announcement. If the crashed engine was the leader, the
cluster performs a failover by electing a new leader from among the engines still
alive. Only the current leader may admit an order, and it may do so only while the
book has room. Despite silent crashes and repeated leader failovers, the auction
must never let the order book grow beyond its fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of orders admitted to the auction book never exceeds the fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m4p0t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
Jobs   == {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
QMax   == 2

VARIABLES queue, lifting

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ lifting = {}

Enqueue(j) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < QMax
    /\ \A i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] # j
    /\ j \notin lifting
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
    /\ UNCHANGED lifting

StartLift ==
    /\ lifting = {}
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ lifting' = {Head(queue)}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

FinishLift(j) ==
    /\ j \in lifting
    /\ lifting' = lifting \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

AdminAbort ==
    /\ lifting # {}
    /\ lifting' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Enqueue(j) \/ FinishLift(j)
    \/ StartLift
    \/ AdminAbort

OneJobLiftedAtATime == \A a, b \in lifting : a = b

vars == <<queue, lifting>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OneJobLiftedAtATime
nl:
A container-ship crane yard feeds lift jobs to a single gantry crane through a
bounded work queue. New jobs are placed on the queue, but the queue applies
backpressure: when it is full, no further jobs may be enqueued until space frees up.
The crane is the critical resource -- it can physically lift only one container at a
time, so at most one job may be in the lifting state. A job moves from the queue into
lifting when the crane is idle, and leaves lifting when the container is set down. A
privileged yard administrator holds an override that can abort whatever is currently
being lifted and clear it, for emergencies. No matter how jobs are enqueued or forced
by the override, the crane must never be lifting two container jobs simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The crane is never lifting more than one container job at the same time.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m4p2t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Total == 4
QMax  == 2

VARIABLES pool, queue, printing, done

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ queue = 0
    /\ printing = 0
    /\ done = 0

ToQueue ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ queue < QMax
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ queue' = queue + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printing, done>>

ToPrinter ==
    /\ queue > 0
    /\ queue' = queue - 1
    /\ printing' = printing + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, done>>

ToDone ==
    /\ printing > 0
    /\ printing' = printing - 1
    /\ done' = done + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queue>>

AdminRecycle ==
    /\ done > 0
    /\ done' = done - 1
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, printing>>

Next == ToQueue \/ ToPrinter \/ ToDone \/ AdminRecycle

JobsConserved == pool + queue + printing + done = Total

vars == <<pool, queue, printing, done>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT JobsConserved
nl:
A print shop moves a fixed set of print jobs through four stages: an intake pool, a
bounded ready queue, the printer, and a done tray. Jobs are never created or destroyed
-- each one is always in exactly one stage and simply advances. The ready queue applies
backpressure: a job may leave the pool for the queue only while the queue holds fewer
jobs than its limit. From the queue a job goes to the printer, and from the printer to
the done tray. A privileged shop administrator has an override that recycles a finished
job from the done tray straight back to the intake pool without going through the queue.
Because every operation merely relocates a job, the total number of jobs across all four
stages must always equal the fixed number the shop started with.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total count of jobs across the pool, queue, printer, and done tray always equals the fixed starting total.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m3p1t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Hubs    == {"h1", "h2"}
Updates == {"u1", "u2"}

VARIABLES leader, pending, log, acked

TypeInv ==
    /\ leader \in Hubs \cup {"none"}
    /\ pending \subseteq Updates
    /\ log \subseteq Updates
    /\ acked \subseteq Updates

Init ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ log = {}
    /\ acked = {}

Elect(h) ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ leader' = h
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, log, acked>>

Failover(h) ==
    /\ leader # "none"
    /\ h # leader
    /\ leader' = h
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, log, acked>>

Propose(u) ==
    /\ u \notin log
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, log, acked>>

Apply(u) ==
    /\ leader # "none"
    /\ u \in pending
    /\ log' = log \cup {u}
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {u}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED leader

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : Elect(h) \/ Failover(h)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Propose(u) \/ Apply(u)

NoLostUpdate == acked \subseteq log

vars == <<leader, pending, log, acked>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network keeps a shared configuration record for its locks. One
hub is elected leader and is the only node allowed to durably apply configuration
updates; if the leader becomes unreachable the network fails over and elects a new
leader. A client proposes an update, which sits as pending until the leader durably
records it in the shared log and acknowledges it back to the client. Nodes may be slow
-- the leader can lag before applying a pending update -- but they do not fail outright,
so a pending update is always eventually handled. The danger with leader changes and
slow application is a lost update: a change the network acknowledged to a client but
that never made it into the durable log. Every acknowledged update must be present in
the durable log.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every update acknowledged to a client is contained in the durable log, so no acknowledged update is ever lost.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m6p6t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Bays    == {"bayN", "bayS"}
Cranes  == {"k1", "k2"}
Lease   == 2
MaxT    == 3

VARIABLES owner, deadline, clock, opened, controller

Init ==
    /\ owner = [b \in Bays |-> "none"]
    /\ deadline = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ opened = Bays
    /\ controller = [b \in Bays |-> "none"]

Acquire(k, b) ==
    /\ b \in opened
    /\ owner[b] = "none"
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = k]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![b] = clock + Lease]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, opened, controller>>

Operate(k, b) ==
    /\ owner[b] = k
    /\ deadline[b] > clock
    /\ controller' = [controller EXCEPT ![b] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, deadline, clock, opened>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ owner' = [b \in Bays |-> IF deadline[b] <= clock + 1 THEN "none" ELSE owner[b]]
    /\ controller' = [b \in Bays |-> IF deadline[b] <= clock + 1 THEN "none" ELSE controller[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deadline, opened>>

CloseBay(b) ==
    /\ b \in opened
    /\ opened' = opened \ {b}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = "none"]
    /\ controller' = [controller EXCEPT ![b] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deadline, clock>>

OpenBay(b) ==
    /\ b \notin opened
    /\ opened' = opened \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, deadline, clock, controller>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Cranes, b \in Bays : Acquire(k, b) \/ Operate(k, b)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E b \in Bays : CloseBay(b) \/ OpenBay(b)

NoStaleControl ==
    \A b \in Bays :
        controller[b] # "none" =>
            (owner[b] = controller[b] /\ deadline[b] > clock)

vars == <<owner, deadline, clock, opened, controller>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleControl
nl:
A container-ship crane yard grants cranes short-lived leases on loading bays. A crane
acquires a lease on a free, open bay, and the lease is stamped with a deadline a fixed
number of clock ticks ahead. Only the crane holding a currently valid lease on a bay
may operate in it, recording itself as that bay's controller. A shared clock advances
one tick at a time; when it passes a lease's deadline, that lease expires and both its
ownership and any control it granted are cleared. The yard changes capacity at runtime
by closing bays out of service or reopening them, which also clears any lease on a
closed bay. The hazard is a stale actor: a crane whose lease has expired must have no
authority. Only a crane holding a live, unexpired lease may be the controller of a bay.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any bay under active control is controlled by the holder of a currently valid, unexpired lease on that bay.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m9p0t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Nodes    == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES inEngine, epoch, inService

Init ==
    /\ inEngine = {}
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ inService = Nodes

Enter(n) ==
    /\ n \in inService
    /\ inEngine = {}
    /\ inEngine' = {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService>>

Exit(n) ==
    /\ n \in inEngine
    /\ inEngine' = inEngine \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ inEngine' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED inService

Activate(n) ==
    /\ n \notin inService
    /\ inService' = inService \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inEngine, epoch>>

Deactivate(n) ==
    /\ n \in inService
    /\ inService' = inService \ {n}
    /\ inEngine' = inEngine \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Next ==
    \E n \in Nodes :
        Enter(n) \/ Exit(n) \/ Activate(n) \/ Deactivate(n) \/ Reconfigure

ExclusiveCross == \A a, b \in inEngine : a = b

matching node may occupy at a time -- it is a critical section. Nodes enter the engine

into service or taken out; only an in-service node may enter the engine, and taking a

ever inside the cross-engine at the same time.

most one slot, tracked as an assignment from robots to slots. A robot claims a free slot

an epoch-numbered reconfiguration, which increments the epoch and releases every current
assignment so the layout can be recomputed from scratch. A privileged warehouse
administrator holds an override that can forcibly reassign a slot to a chosen robot,
first pulling it from whoever held it, to resolve conflicts by hand. Robots can also
release slots they hold. Despite epoch reconfigurations and the admin override, the
system must never let the same charging slot be assigned to two different robots at once.

outward. Trains occupy blocks and advance one block at a time toward the far end. Two

movement authority; either controller lets a train step forward into the next block only
when that block is currently unoccupied. Occasionally the line performs an epoch-numbered
reconfiguration that bumps the epoch and resets every train back to its distinct starting
block so the interlocking can be recomputed. Because two controllers drive the same
trains over the same blocks, the cardinal safety rule is collision avoidance: no signalling
block may ever hold two trains at once.

nl:

enter, being washed on the conveyor, and finished. A controller sequences the conveyor,
and one controller is elected leader; only the leader advances cars. If the leader
becomes unavailable the line fails over and elects a new leader from the standby
controllers. The leader may be slow -- it can pause between advancing cars -- but it does
not fail while acting. A car moves from waiting onto the conveyor to be washed, then from
the conveyor to finished; nothing else creates or removes cars. Because every step just
relocates a car among the three stages, the total number of cars on the line must remain
exactly the number that started.

changes at runtime: cars go out of service for maintenance and later return, and taking a
car out of service drops whatever call it was handling back for reassignment. The core
safety requirement is that a single hall call is never being served by two different
elevators at the same time.

An air-traffic runway allocator hands out a fixed pool of runway time-slots using a
two-phase commit across control towers. The coordinator proposes moving a slot from the
free pool into a pending reservation; the towers vote, and on unanimous commit the slot
becomes allocated, while an abort returns the pending slot to the free pool. An allocated slot is later released back
to the free pool once its runway time has elapsed. Any single
tower may crash silently -- it simply stops voting -- but a slot in flight is never
duplicated or dropped: it is always in exactly one of the free pool, the pending
reservation, or the allocated set. Across proposals, votes, commits, aborts, and silent
tower crashes, the total number of runway slots must remain exactly the fixed pool size.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of runway slots across the free pool, pending reservations, and allocated set always equals the fixed pool size.

A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker maintains a lobby roster of committed players using a
two-phase commit. Adding a player first prepares the addition, then commits it, at which
point the player is durably recorded both in the committed set and in the live roster; a
prepared addition may instead be aborted before commit. The lobby's maximum size changes
at runtime as the host resizes it, and a commit is allowed only while the roster is below
the current maximum. Players may also leave, which removes them from the live roster and
from the committed set together. The hazard is a lost update: a player the matchmaker
committed but who is missing from the live roster. Every committed player must appear in
the live roster.

nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction over a ring of nodes that pass a single access
token around. Only the node currently holding the token may admit orders into the auction
book, which has a strictly bounded capacity counted as the number of admitted orders. To
pass the token a node emits a token message flagged for a destination node; these messages
travel over an asynchronous network and may be delivered in any order, so several token
messages can be pending at once and arrive reordered. While the token is traveling no node
holds it. A node becomes the holder when it receives a pending token message. Only a holder
may admit an order, and only while the admitted-order count is still below capacity. Despite
reordered token messages and repeated hand-offs, the auction book must never grow beyond its
fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of orders admitted to the auction book never exceeds the fixed capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m4p2t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Start == 2

QMax  == 2

VARIABLES bal, queue

TypeInv ==
    /\ bal \in [Banks -> 0..Total]
    /\ queue \in Seq([from: Banks, to: Banks])

Init ==
    /\ bal = [b \in Banks |-> Start]
    /\ queue = << >>

Submit(f, t) ==
    /\ f # t
    /\ Len(queue) < QMax
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [from |-> f, to |-> t])
    /\ UNCHANGED bal

Process ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ bal[Head(queue).from] >= Amt
    /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![Head(queue).from] = @ - Amt,
                          ![Head(queue).to]   = @ + Amt]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

Reject ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ bal[Head(queue).from] < Amt
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED bal

Cancel(i) ==
    /\ i \in DOMAIN queue
    /\ queue' = SubSeq(queue, 1, i - 1) \o SubSeq(queue, i + 1, Len(queue))
    /\ UNCHANGED bal

    \/ \E f, t \in Banks : Submit(f, t)
    \/ Process \/ Reject
    \/ \E i \in DOMAIN queue : Cancel(i)

nl:

instructions -- each moving a fixed amount from one bank to another -- arrive on a bounded
work queue that applies backpressure: when the queue is full, no new instruction may be
submitted until one is drained. A settlement engine processes the instruction at the head
of the queue by debiting the sender and crediting the receiver, provided the sender has
sufficient funds; an instruction whose sender lacks funds is rejected and dropped, and a
queued instruction may also be cancelled. The engine may be slow, letting instructions sit
in the queue, but it does not fail. Because every processed settlement moves money without
creating or destroying it, the total funds held across all member banks must stay constant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total funds summed across all member banks always equals the fixed starting total.

independent dispatchers share the same pool of boarding requests. To board a rider a
dispatcher first prepares a reservation, which tentatively holds a seat, and then commits

occupants plus outstanding reservations are still below the car's capacity, so the two

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m5p3t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

    /\ proposal \in [{"req", "elev"} -> Requests \cup Elevators \cup {"none"}]
    /\ votes \subseteq Controllers

    /\ assign = [r \in Requests |-> "none"]
    /\ proposal = [x \in {"req", "elev"} |-> "none"]
    /\ votes = {}

    /\ proposal["req"] = "none"
    /\ assign[r] = "none"
    /\ \A q \in Requests : assign[q] # e
    /\ proposal' = [req |-> r, elev |-> e]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED assign

CastVote(c) ==
    /\ proposal["req"] # "none"
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assign, proposal>>

Commit ==
    /\ proposal["req"] # "none"
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ \A q \in Requests : assign[q] # proposal["elev"]
    /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![proposal["req"]] = proposal["elev"]]
    /\ proposal' = [x \in {"req", "elev"} |-> "none"]
    /\ votes' = {}

Abandon ==
    /\ proposal["req"] # "none"
    /\ proposal' = [x \in {"req", "elev"} |-> "none"]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED assign

Release(r) ==
    /\ assign[r] # "none"
    /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![r] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes>>

agrees. To assign a request the system opens a single proposal naming a request and a
candidate elevator; controllers then cast votes for that proposal, and once a quorum of
votes is reached the assignment is committed. A proposal may also be abandoned before it
reaches quorum. Controllers may be slow to vote -- a proposal can linger while votes trickle
in -- but they do not fail. A committed assignment binds a request to an elevator, and an
assignment is released when the request is served. The proposal machinery must ensure that
no single elevator is ever committed to serve two different floor requests at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No elevator is ever assigned to two different floor requests at the same time.

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares one fast-charging station that only a single robot may
occupy at a time. Two independent fleet controllers dispatch robots to the charger without a
shared lock, using optimistic concurrency instead. A controller first snapshots the
station's version number, then tries to move its robot onto the charger only if the version
it saw still matches the live version; a successful entry bumps the version. If another
controller changed the station in between, the snapshot is stale and the entry attempt is
retried against the refreshed version. A robot leaves the charger when done, again bumping
the version. Because two controllers race optimistically over the same station, the safety
requirement is strict mutual exclusion: at most one robot may occupy the charger at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one robot ever occupies the charging station at the same time.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m2p5t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
Matches == {"m1", "m2"}

VARIABLES phase, startLog, everStarted

TypeInv ==
    /\ phase \in [Matches -> {"open", "prepared", "started"}]
    /\ startLog \in Seq(Matches)
    /\ everStarted \subseteq Matches

Init ==
    /\ phase = [m \in Matches |-> "open"]
    /\ startLog = << >>
    /\ everStarted = {}

Prepare(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "open"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "prepared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<startLog, everStarted>>

Commit(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "prepared"
    /\ m \notin everStarted
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "started"]
    /\ startLog' = Append(startLog, m)
    /\ everStarted' = everStarted \cup {m}

AbortToOpen(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "prepared"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "open"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<startLog, everStarted>>

Teardown(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "started"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "open"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<startLog, everStarted>>

Next ==
    \E m \in Matches :
        Prepare(m) \/ Commit(m) \/ AbortToOpen(m) \/ Teardown(m)

EachMatchStartsOnce ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN startLog : startLog[i] = startLog[j] => i = j

vars == <<phase, startLog, everStarted>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT EachMatchStartsOnce
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker finalizes matches through a two-phase commit. A match
first prepares -- gathering its players and locking their entry stakes -- and then commits,
at which point the match is physically started: stakes are charged and the game server is
spun up, and this start is recorded in an ordered start log. Starting a match is
irreversible in the sense that a given match may be started only once, even though its
server can later be torn down and the lobby reopened. Any single player may crash silently
during the protocol, dropping out and causing the prepared match to be aborted back to the
open state instead of started. The essential guarantee is that the irreversible start of any
given match happens at most once, so no match identifier is ever recorded twice in the start
log and no player is charged twice for the same match.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No match is ever started more than once, i.e. no match identifier appears twice in the start log.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m2p5t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Doors == {"front", "back"}

VARIABLES phase, events, nextSeq

TypeInv ==
    /\ phase \in [Doors -> {"idle", "prepared", "unlocked"}]
    /\ events \subseteq [door: Doors, seq: 0..4]
    /\ nextSeq \in 0..4

FiredDoors == {e.door : e \in events}

Init ==
    /\ phase = [d \in Doors |-> "idle"]
    /\ events = {}
    /\ nextSeq = 0

Prepare(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "prepared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<events, nextSeq>>

Commit(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "prepared"
    /\ d \notin FiredDoors
    /\ nextSeq < 4
    /\ events' = events \cup {[door |-> d, seq |-> nextSeq]}
    /\ nextSeq' = nextSeq + 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "unlocked"]

Abort(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "prepared"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<events, nextSeq>>

Relock(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "unlocked"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<events, nextSeq>>

Next ==
    \E d \in Doors : Prepare(d) \/ Commit(d) \/ Abort(d) \/ Relock(d)

AtMostOneUnlockPerDoor ==
    \A e1, e2 \in events : e1.door = e2.door => e1 = e2

vars == <<phase, events, nextSeq>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneUnlockPerDoor
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network authorizes a guest entry through a two-phase commit across
the door node and the hub. An entry is first prepared, then committed, and only on commit
does the physical latch fire to unlock the door -- an irreversible actuation that consumes a
single-use entry credential. Each actuation is recorded as an event stamped with a unique
sequence number. The nodes may be slow, letting a prepared entry sit before it commits or
aborts, but they do not fail. After an entry the door can be relocked and a fresh session
opened, yet the single-use credential for a given door may fire its latch only once. The
network must guarantee that the irreversible latch actuation for any one door is never
recorded more than once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For each door, at most one latch-actuation event is ever recorded.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m8p3t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
Students == {"s1", "s2"}
Seats    == {"seatA", "seatB"}

VARIABLES deptLock, seatLock, seatOf

TypeInv ==
    /\ deptLock \in Students \cup {"free"}
    /\ seatLock \in [Seats -> Students \cup {"free"}]
    /\ seatOf \in [Students -> Seats \cup {"none"}]

Init ==
    /\ deptLock = "free"
    /\ seatLock = [s \in Seats |-> "free"]
    /\ seatOf = [st \in Students |-> "none"]

TakeDept(st) ==
    /\ deptLock = "free"
    /\ deptLock' = st
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seatLock, seatOf>>

TakeSeatLock(st, se) ==
    /\ deptLock = st
    /\ seatLock[se] = "free"
    /\ seatLock' = [seatLock EXCEPT ![se] = st]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, seatOf>>

Enroll(st, se) ==
    /\ seatLock[se] = st
    /\ seatOf[st] = "none"
    /\ \A o \in Students : seatOf[o] # se
    /\ seatOf' = [seatOf EXCEPT ![st] = se]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, seatLock>>

ReleaseLocks(st, se) ==
    /\ deptLock = st
    /\ seatLock[se] = st
    /\ seatLock' = [seatLock EXCEPT ![se] = "free"]
    /\ deptLock' = "free"
    /\ UNCHANGED seatOf

Drop(st) ==
    /\ seatOf[st] # "none"
    /\ seatOf' = [seatOf EXCEPT ![st] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, seatLock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E st \in Students : TakeDept(st) \/ Drop(st)
    \/ \E st \in Students, se \in Seats :
        TakeSeatLock(st, se) \/ Enroll(st, se) \/ ReleaseLocks(st, se)

NoSeatDoubleAssigned ==
    \A a, b \in Students :
        (seatOf[a] # "none" /\ seatOf[a] = seatOf[b]) => a = b

vars == <<deptLock, seatLock, seatOf>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoSeatDoubleAssigned
nl:
A university course-registration system seats students using a two-level hierarchical lock:
to enroll a student a registrar must first take the coarse lock on the department, then the
fine lock on the specific course seat, and only then bind that seat to the student. Two
independent registration front-ends share the same pool of seats and students, each taking
locks and enrolling on its own. A seat may be bound to a student only when no other student
currently holds it. After enrollment a registrar releases both locks, and a student may drop
a seat, freeing it. Because two front-ends contend for the same seats through the lock
hierarchy, the registrar must ensure that a single course seat is never bound to two
different students at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No course seat is ever bound to two different students at the same time.
